topic: Measurement design as the argument of the semiparametric efficiency bound for long-term treatment effects in the Imbens-Kallus-Mao-Wang long-term data-combination model, with a finite costed catalogue of candidate short-term outcomes, admissible measured-subset and role-assignment pairs, and budget allocation between experimental and long-term-follow-up samples.

open_problems.open_problem: Does selecting an admissible short-term-outcome design by predictive accuracy for the long-term outcome have any finite approximation guarantee for the budget-normalized semiparametric efficiency bound, or can its design-value ratio be unbounded even when every candidate design is regular?

source_refs.claim: The paper fixes the short-term-outcome groups and sample composition and derives local efficiency only after the measurement system is given.
source_refs.author: Guido Imbens, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Yuhao Wang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The authors show that highly outcome-predictive surrogates need not have high policy value because predicting outcome levels differs from predicting treatment effects.
source_refs.author: Jeremy Yang, Dean Eckles, Paramveer Dhillon, Sinan Aral

source_refs.claim: For covariate choice in a randomized trial, the precision-cost problem is equivalent to budget-constrained outcome prediction, an equivalence not established for bridge-based data fusion.
source_refs.author: Pedro Carneiro, Sokbae Lee, Daniel Wilhelm

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prediction is efficiency-aligned for ordinary randomized regression adjustment, and predictive surrogates improve efficiency in a fixed-surrogate missing-outcome model, but persistent-confounding data fusion has two inverse bridge problems and a role assignment among sequential outcome groups. Prediction risk controls neither the relevant inverse-operator geometry nor the two sample-specific components of the efficient influence function, so the literature supplies no comparison inequality between predictive risk and the design-indexed efficiency bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a sharp approximation-ratio theorem under named operator conditions or an open-set counterexample theorem giving an unbounded predictive-to-optimal design-value ratio while every admissible design remains regular.

writing_exemplar.why: Its persistent-confounding setup, sequential proxy roles, and bridge-based efficiency analysis are exactly the model into which measurement choice must be inserted.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: long-term outcomes are absent from experiments -> observational long-term outcomes are persistently confounded -> sequential short-term outcomes restore regular estimation -> does prediction-based proxy selection control the resulting efficiency bound?

method_exemplars.technique: Rewrite cost-normalized asymptotic variance as a subset-selection objective and analyze a pilot-fitted selector via variance decomposition and budget feasibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves prediction-efficiency equivalence in the nearest model where prediction is the correct criterion, providing the benchmark whose failure or modification must be established.

method_exemplars.technique: Use penalized minimax estimation of primal and debiasing functions and prove root-n inference for a strongly identified linear functional despite ill-posed or nonunique nuisance solutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The long-term ATE is likewise a functional of bridge solutions; this machinery isolates the operator quantities that predictive accuracy fails to control.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact design-value ordering criterion over a finite admissible family of measured-subset and sequential-role assignments in the persistent-confounding long-term model?

source_refs.claim: The paper discusses competing consequences of richer intermediate-outcome groups but does not compare efficiency bounds across alternative measured subsets and role partitions.
source_refs.author: Guido Imbens, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Yuhao Wang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper compares efficiency with and without a fixed surrogate set and relates gains to predictive surrogates, but does not optimize over costly sets or causal roles.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper derives efficiency-oriented phase-two sampling for a fixed expensive-variable problem; its design variable is the sampling rule, not which variables and bridge roles are measured.
source_refs.author: Ran Tao, Donglin Zeng, Dan-Yu Lin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adding a variable within a fixed coarsening model ordinarily enlarges information, but changing an outcome's sequential role changes the conditional-moment operators, bridge domains, nuisance tangent space, and both canonical-gradient components. Candidate role assignments therefore are not nested statistical experiments, so neither Blackwell monotonicity nor ordinary conditional-variance ordering supplies the comparison; existing surrogate-efficiency and two-phase-design papers keep either the variable set or its role fixed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient comparison theorem expressing the design-value gap between two regular subset-role assignments as identified quadratic forms or canonical-gradient projection norms.

writing_exemplar.why: Its three-role sequential setup makes clear why a measured variable is not merely added information but can enter a different inverse problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: sequential outcomes play distinct bridge roles -> those roles determine identification and the canonical gradient -> candidate measurements can be assigned to different roles -> what identified criterion orders their efficiency?

method_exemplars.technique: Compare canonical-gradient variances across coarsening maps and reduce efficiency gains to conditional-variance components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest published efficiency-gap calculation for surrogate information, though the new comparison must allow bridge roles to change.

method_exemplars.technique: Expose how a design parameter enters the semiparametric information bound, optimize the criterion, and couple it with an efficient estimator and limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is likewise an efficiency bound with design as an argument, but over discrete measurement-role designs rather than phase-two inclusion probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: For each regular measurement design, what is the cost-optimal allocation of units between the randomized short-term sample and the observational long-term-follow-up sample, and how does profiling this allocation change the globally optimal measurement design?

source_refs.claim: The efficient influence function has distinct experimental- and observational-sample contributions, but the sampling ratio is treated as exogenously fixed.
source_refs.author: Guido Imbens, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Yuhao Wang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper observes that data-fusion datasets are usually treated as given and shows in a general moment model that optimal budget allocation across sources depends on the unknown law.
source_refs.author: Shantanu Gupta, Zachary C. Lipton, David Childers

source_refs.claim: The paper minimizes a semiparametric efficiency bound over a phase-two sampling rule under a budget fraction while holding the measured-variable system fixed.
source_refs.author: Ruoyu Wang, Qihua Wang, Wang Miao

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two sample-specific influence-function variances suggest a Neyman-type square-root allocation, but their values depend on the chosen proxy subset and role assignment, while measurement and long-term-follow-up costs also vary by design. The bridge nuisances are learned from different sources, so boundary allocations can destroy the rates needed for regularity even when each fixed interior design is regular; existing moment-allocation and two-phase-sampling results do not derive this profile for the coupled bridge model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit budget-allocation profile and optimizer theorem, including boundary regularity conditions, followed by a joint finite-family minimization theorem for the profiled design value.

writing_exemplar.why: It already separates the experimental and observational influence-function contributions, making allocation the natural next design variable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: two complementary samples are both necessary -> each contributes a different variance component -> their units have different costs -> what allocation minimizes the cost-normalized efficiency bound for each measurement design?

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize asymptotic MSE over costed source-query frequencies and prove oracle-regret guarantees for adaptive allocation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its source-frequency decision is structurally the same as choosing the experimental-observational budget split once this model's efficient moments are supplied.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a design-indexed efficient influence function, solve constrained efficiency-bound minimization, and estimate the oracle rule from a pilot.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest semiparametric proof template for profiling an efficiency bound over a cost-constrained collection rule.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a full-catalogue pilot support a feasible plug-in selector of the measurement design whose design-value regret vanishes and whose subsequent long-term ATE estimator has valid post-selection inference?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves zero asymptotic-MSE regret for source allocation learned from accumulating data, but does not select proxy subsets or bridge roles.
source_refs.author: Shantanu Gupta, Zachary C. Lipton, David Childers

source_refs.claim: The paper estimates an efficiency-optimal two-phase sampling rule from an initial random pilot and proves near-optimality for a fixed full-data influence function.
source_refs.author: Ruoyu Wang, Qihua Wang, Wang Miao

source_refs.claim: The paper uses pre-experimental full-catalogue data to select a cost-constrained covariate set and sample size for a randomized trial using an outcome-prediction objective.
source_refs.author: Pedro Carneiro, Sokbae Lee, Daniel Wilhelm

open_problems.why_unsolved: For a finite catalogue, pointwise consistency of each estimated bound is insufficient near ties: selection needs uniform control of bridge estimators, inverse-operator regularization, estimated canonical-gradient variances, and the allocation profile. Reusing the pilot can also create selection-induced first-order terms. Existing pilot-optimal designs assume a fixed full-data influence function or prediction loss, whereas every subset-role candidate here has its own nuisance equations and canonical gradient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform plug-in design-value consistency theorem, a finite-family oracle-regret bound with explicit tie handling, and a sample-split or orthogonalized post-selection central limit theorem with consistently estimated variance.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation turns data-fusion sources from fixed inputs into a learnable collection policy, exactly the arc needed for a pilot-based measurement rule.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: data-fusion efficiency assumes sources are already collected -> optimal collection depends on the unknown law -> a pilot can learn the design objective -> can it select proxy subsets and roles with oracle regret and valid ATE inference?

method_exemplars.technique: Use a shrinking pilot to estimate conditional influence-function variances, enforce the budget, and bound the distance between learned and oracle sampling rules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest pilot-to-efficient-design theorem, but must be lifted from one continuous sampling rule to a finite family of bridge-defined designs.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct penalized minimax primal and debiasing nuisances with fixed regularized limits, then prove asymptotic linearity of the target functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform pilot evaluation of each candidate requires stable bridge-functional estimation even when bridge equations are ill-posed or nonunique.

open_problems.open_problem: How should the local semiparametric efficiency bound for the long-term ATE be characterized when candidate measurement designs induce nonunique bridge functions, and can that characterization explain efficiency deterioration after adding otherwise regular proxies?

source_refs.claim: The paper states that bridge nonuniqueness matters for inference and proves its efficiency bound under bridge uniqueness and operator-bijectivity conditions.
source_refs.author: Guido Imbens, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Yuhao Wang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper gives root-n inference for strongly identified linear functionals when conditional-moment nuisance functions are ill-posed or nonunique, but not the long-term data-combination efficiency bound.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Proximal causal functionals can remain identified without unique bridge solutions, so bridge nonuniqueness need not itself imply target nonregularity.
source_refs.author: Jinghao Zhang, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen and coauthors

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's uniqueness assumption collapses each bridge solution set to one nuisance and makes its displayed variance canonical. With nonunique solutions, regularizations choose different representatives, and adding proxies can alter null spaces or the dual range even while the ATE remains a strongly identified regular functional. Existing nonunique-bridge work establishes identification or root-n estimation but does not compute the canonical gradient in this two-sample sequential-outcome model or order it across measurement designs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tangent-space or minimum-norm characterization of the canonical gradient over primal-dual bridge solution sets, together with a regime-specific theorem showing when proxy enlargement raises, lowers, or leaves unchanged the efficiency bound.

writing_exemplar.why: The paper itself isolates bridge nonuniqueness as the obstacle preventing its local-efficiency theorem from covering all identified laws.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: bridge equations identify the long-term ATE -> their solutions need not be unique -> target regularity can survive nuisance nonuniqueness -> what is the canonical efficiency bound and how does measurement expansion change it?

method_exemplars.technique: Use primal and dual bridge existence to show that the causal mean is invariant across bridge solution sets without imposing uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The canonical-gradient characterization first needs the same solution-set invariance for the long-term ATE's coupled bridges.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize strong identification through a debiasing nuisance, select fixed penalized representatives, and prove a root-n asymptotically normal debiased estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly handles continuous linear functionals of nonunique conditional-moment solutions, matching the operator structure of the long-term bridges.

literature_map:
1. Imbens-Kallus-Mao-Wang (JRSSB 2025, arXiv:2202.07234) identify long-term ATEs under persistent confounding using sequential short-term-outcome roles; measurement sets and sample shares are fixed.
2. Their efficiency theorem imposes bridge uniqueness and operator conditions, while their discussion identifies bridge nonuniqueness as consequential for inference.
3. Athey-Chetty-Imbens-Kang (Biometrika 2023; arXiv:1603.09326) combine many short-term proxies through a predictive surrogate index under statistical surrogacy, without costed subset optimization.
4. Chen-Ritzwoller (Journal of Econometrics 2023; arXiv:2107.14405) derive orthogonal estimators for long-term data fusion but treat proxy systems and sample proportions as given.
5. Ghassami-Yang-Richardson-Shpitser-Tchetgen Tchetgen (arXiv:2201.10743) give alternative long-term identification strategies, including proximal fusion, again without measurement design.
6. Hu-Zhou-Wu (Statistica Sinica 2025; arXiv:2208.10163) derive an efficient influence function and locally efficient estimator under mean exchangeability with a fixed surrogate set.
7. Kallus-Mao (JRSSB 2025; arXiv:2003.12408) compare with-versus-without-surrogate efficiency and find larger gains for more predictive fixed surrogates, not optimal selection over costly sets.
8. Yang-Eckles-Dhillon-Aral (Management Science 2024; arXiv:2010.15835) show that outcome prediction need not imply high causal policy value, sharpening the prediction-versus-causal-design tension.
9. Price-Gilbert-van der Laan (Biometrics 2018, DOI 10.1111/biom.12879) define a predictive optimal surrogate but require randomized long-term outcomes and do not optimize an efficiency bound.
10. Wang-Parast-Tian-Cai (arXiv:2209.08414) optimize a transformation of a given surrogate for power, not the measured subset, causal role, or two-sample budget.
11. Carneiro-Lee-Wilhelm (Econometrics Journal 2020, DOI 10.1093/ectj/utz020) make prediction equivalent to cost-efficient covariate collection in an ordinary RCT; bridge-based fusion falls outside that equivalence.
12. Tao-Zeng-Lin (JASA 2020, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2019.1671200) and Wang-Wang-Miao (arXiv:2312.10596) optimize two-phase inclusion rules for fixed variable systems.
13. Mareis-Drton (CLeaR 2026; arXiv:2603.22024) optimize cost-aware partial measurement in a multivariate linear front-door model, narrower than the nonparametric long-term bridge model.
14. Gupta-Lipton-Childers (arXiv:2411.03195) optimize budget allocation across moment sources and prove oracle regret, furnishing machinery for but not solving proxy subset-role selection.
15. Bennett-Kallus-Mao-Newey-Syrgkanis-Uehara (COLT 2023; arXiv:2208.08291) provide inference for strongly identified functionals of nonunique inverse-problem nuisances, the closest technique for extending the anchor's efficiency analysis.
prior_proposal_map:
Closest source: failed pid_long_term_surrogate/v1; inspected its README, final proposal, both rejected-angle proposals, and all angle0/angle1/angle2 reviewer JSONs.
Its final reviewer identified three live repairs: a K=2,J=1 strict-tightening theorem, common-kernel bridge compatibility, or a sharp no-extra-information counterexample.
Second high-signal source: failed eid_proximal_completeness/v1; inspected its README, final proposal, four rejected angles, and all reviewer JSONs.
Its rejected angle1 proposed proxy-panel choice by target-relevant common-kernel width rather than prediction, but left causal realization and boundary geometry open.
Its final angle left a uniform strong/weak/failed-completeness confidence-set phase diagram open; reviewers requested a computable index and Le Cam converse.
Adjacent READMEs inspected: downgraded eid_proximal_phase/v1, failed pid_surrogate_paradox_phase/v1, downgraded stat_ddd_overid_efficiency/v1, and accepted rollout-design banks.
The surrogate-paradox bank mainly records algebraic dead ends; the DDD bank leaves a generic full semiparametric-bound extension but is not long-term specific.
No prior reviewer JSON directly settled efficiency-optimal subset selection, predictive-selection approximation guarantees, or optimal experimental/long-follow-up allocation in the Imbens-Kallus-Mao-Wang model.
